newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks show signs of bottoming out-brokers.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks show signs of bottoming out-brokers.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks, which backtracked after reaching 630 points in mid-October on profit-taking by retail investors, are showing signs of bottoming out, brokers said.
The all share index was down 1.01 points at 606.68 by the mid-morning break. Turnover was a low 4.3 million rupees.
"Profit-taking by retail investors which brought the index down from 630 points, seems to have eased," said K. Anurathan a trader at brokerage CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch.
Low value shares which are favoured by small investors like Vanik, are showing signs of moving up again, he said.
"Volumes are low because of the inactivity among high-priced shares," Anurathan said.
Final turnover, however, is expected to improve marginally when 800,000 shares of Grain Elevators, which is on bid at nine rupees, is concluded, brokers said.
